note: Generated by scripts/build_deals_ontology.py from ontology_v0 + the jp_morgan.csv schema.

terms.name: Acquired Bank (Target)
terms.definition: A bank that ceased to exist in a deal and whose business ended up inside JPMorgan Chase, directly or through a chain of earlier acquisitions. Each row of the deals table is one such bank.

terms.name: Acquirer Bank
terms.definition: The bank that bought a given row's target bank. This is JPMorgan's lead bank only for direct purchases; for indirect purchases it is an intermediate bank that JPMorgan later absorbed.

terms.name: JPMorgan Chase Lead Bank
terms.definition: JPMorgan Chase's own bank charter, FDIC certificate 628, recorded under the historical names Chemical Bank, The Chase Manhattan Bank and JPMorgan Chase Bank, National Association. It is the acquirer in every direct purchase.

terms.name: FDIC Certificate Number
terms.definition: The FDIC's unique bank identifier, stable across bank name changes. Used to identify the same bank across rows and roles (target, acquirer, survivor).

terms.name: Acquisition Path
terms.definition: Whether JPMorgan Chase bought the target itself (direct purchase) or the target was bought by a bank that JPMorgan later absorbed (indirect purchase).

terms.name: Direct Purchase
terms.definition: A target bank bought by JPMorgan Chase's own lead bank; generation 1.

terms.name: Indirect Purchase
terms.definition: A target bank bought by another bank that JPMorgan Chase later absorbed (generation 2 to 7).
aliases: bought by a bank later absorbed

terms.name: Acquisition Generation
terms.definition: Number of steps from the target bank up to JPMorgan Chase in the family tree: 1 = bought directly, 2 = bought by a bank JPMorgan later bought, and so on up to 7.

terms.name: Acquisition Chain
terms.definition: The ordered list of banks from the target up to JPMorgan Chase's lead bank, showing through which intermediate banks the target arrived.

terms.name: Deal Category
terms.definition: Broad deal group: Voluntary M&A (purchase between healthy banks) or Assisted / failed-bank deal (a failing bank sold or merged with FDIC involvement).

terms.name: Failed-Bank / FDIC-Assisted Deal
terms.definition: A deal in which a failing bank was sold, merged with FDIC assistance, or passed through a receivership, conservatorship or bridge bank.

terms.name: Voluntary M&A
terms.definition: An ordinary merger, consolidation or absorption between healthy banks.

terms.name: Deal Type
terms.definition: Plain-language kind of deal (Merger, Consolidation, Absorption, Assisted merger, Failure - whole institution acquired, Failure - passthrough receivership/conservatorship, Failure - acquired by bidder, Failure - bridge bank).

terms.name: Deal Year
terms.definition: Calendar year in which the deal took effect.

terms.name: Deal Decade
terms.definition: Ten-year period (1970s ... 2020s) of the deal's effective year.

terms.name: Target Assets Before Deal
terms.definition: Total assets of the acquired bank in its last quarterly report before the deal; the main measure of acquisition size.

terms.name: Deal Price
terms.definition: Price recorded for the deal in this file.

terms.name: Target State
terms.definition: Two-letter state code of the acquired bank's head office at the time of the deal.

constraints.description: Missing numeric values are stored as empty strings, not NULL. In SQLite, text sorts above every number, so a descending sort puts blank rows first; averages treat blanks as 0 (target assets: 2,421,034 with blanks vs 2,854,429 without). Missing values must be excluded or treated as NULL before ranking or averaging.
Columns ending in _000 are in thousands of dollars (232,944,161 = $232.9 billion). deal_price_usd is in whole dollars. Do not mix the two without converting.

deal_price_usd holds random placeholder values (file name: jpmorgan_chase_deals_with_random_prices.csv; range 135,000 to 49,946,000 dollars even for $300B banks). Price results describe the synthetic file, not real deal values, and must be reported with that caveat.

The acquirer columns describe the bank that bought that row's target, which is JPMorgan's lead bank only for the 29 direct purchases. For the other 926 rows the acquirer is an intermediate bank later absorbed by JPMorgan. 'Banks JPMorgan acquired' includes all 955 rows unless the question asks specifically for direct purchases.

Bank names change over time while the FDIC certificate stays the same: 295 distinct acquirer certificates vs 368 distinct acquirer names. Certificate 628 appears as Chemical Bank (13 rows), The Chase Manhattan Bank (6) and JPMorgan Chase Bank, National Association (10). Count per certificate, not per name, to avoid splitting one bank.

Failed-bank / FDIC-assisted deals are the 238 rows with deal category 'Assisted / failed-bank deal' (Failure - whole institution acquired 164, passthrough receivership/conservatorship 43, Assisted merger 18, acquired by bidder 9, bridge bank 4). The failure_* columns are filled for only 195 of them, so they must not be used to identify or count failed-bank deals. Use the deal year (year / effective_date) for timing, since failure_date is missing for 43 of these rows.

Pre-deal assets are missing for 145 rows, mostly deals before 1984 when quarterly reports begin (blank rows span 1970-2003; 22 blank rows from 1984 on). Size rankings cover only deals with a reported value; say so in the answer.
Generation 1 = direct purchase (29), 2 = 151, 3 = 332, 4 = 287, 5 = 117, 6 = 37, 7 = 2. Generation >= 2 is indirect.

Deals run from 1970-07-17 to 2023-05-01 and are concentrated in the 1980s (409) and 1990s (441); the 2000s have 40, the 2010s 3 and the 2020s 1. Decades with few deals give small totals because of low counts, not because of smaller deals.
